entities.summary: The Lordship of Prilep, also known as the Realm of King Marko or the Kingdom of Prilep, was one of the successor-states of the Serbian Empire, covering mainly the southern regions of the former empire, corresponding to western parts of present-day North Macedonia. Its central region of Pelagonia, with the city of Prilep, was held by lord Vukašin Mrnjavčević, who in 1365 became Serbian king and co-ruler of Serbian emperor Stefan Uroš V (1355–1371). After king Vukašin died at the Battle of Maritsa in 1371, the realm was obtained by his son and designated successor Marko Mrnjavčević, who took the title of Serbian king.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Lordship of Prilep played a significant role in the succession of Serbian emperors after the Battle of Maritsa in 1371, with its ruler Marko Mrnjavčević becoming Serbian king and co-ruler of Stefan Uroš V. This led to a shift in regional power dynamics.
